question: When do I need to apply for Stamp 1G
reference: Within six months of being notified by the awarding body or institution that you have achieved your award. Provisional results are not sufficient.
answer: You must apply for a Stamp 1G immigration permission within six months of being notified by the relevant awarding body or institution that you have achieved the award for which you had enrolled as a student [1]. You can only qualify for a Stamp 1G permission after your provider has issued final results and you can evidence that you have achieved the award [1]. Provisional results will not suffice [1].

question: I just finished my masters can I stay in Ireland and look for a job
reference: Yes, if eligible, under the Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G), which lets graduates stay after their studies to look for graduate-level employment, subject to conditions such as applying within six months of being notified of the award.
answer: You may be eligible to remain in Ireland under the Third Level Graduate Programme, which allows you to stay for 12 months after completing your studies [1]. However, you must register with Immigration Service Delivery if you are from outside the EU, UK or Switzerland and have been in Ireland for more than 90 days [2].

Not wrong: source [1] gives twelve months for Level 8/9 graduates, and the reference's main point (yes, via the Third Level Graduate Programme) is made. Omission treated as a minor detail, not misleading. Also omits job-seeking and the six-month application deadline. faithful=1: statements match [1] and [2] and apply to the same situation.

question: How long is the graduate permission for a level 9 masters degree
reference: 12 months initially, renewable for a further 12 months (24 months in total) if you show you have taken steps to find graduate-level employment, subject to the overall eight-year limit.
answer:
Graduates with an award at Level 9 or above on the National Framework of Qualifications who qualify for the Programme will be granted permission for 12 months initially [1]. This will be renewed for a further period of twelve months (subject to the overall eight year limit on student conditions not being exceeded) where the graduate satisfies the immigration authorities that he or she has taken appropriate steps to access suitable graduate level employment [1].

Note: The sources do not specify a specific duration for a Level 9 masters degree, but rather provide general information about the Programme.
notes: Adds 'The sources do not specify a specific duration for a Level 9 masters degree' - a note about what the sources don't mention, and it contradicts source [1], which gives 12 months initially plus 12 more for Level 9. Main answer itself is right.

question: What does Stamp 1G allow me to do
reference: Look for employment under the Third Level Graduate Programme. You may work full time but may not operate a business or be self-employed.
answer: Stamp 1G allows you to look for employment in Ireland under the Third Level Graduate Programme, and you can work full time in accordance with employment law requirements [1]. You are not permitted to operate a business or be self-employed [4]. If you wish to continue working after Stamp 1G expires, you must find a job that requires an employment permit [1].

question: What is Stamp 0
reference: Permission to stay in Ireland for a temporary period, subject to conditions such as being financially self-sufficient (or fully supported by a sponsor), no access to benefits or publicly funded services, and having private medical insurance.
answer: Stamp 0 indicates permission to stay in Ireland for a temporary period, subject to conditions [2]. You must be of independent means and fully financially self-sufficient, or your sponsor in Ireland must support you fully [2]. You cannot receive any benefits or use publicly funded services, and you must have private medical insurance [2].

question: Can I work full time during the summer holidays on Stamp 2
reference: You may work up to 40 hours per week during holiday periods (June to September and 15 December to 15 January). During term the limit is 20 hours per week.
answer: Yes, according to [2], you can work in casual employment for a maximum of 40 hours per week during holidays. However, it's not specified that this is limited to part-time work only, so it seems you can work full-time during summer holidays on Stamp 2 [2].
notes: Says 'it's not specified that this is limited to part-time work only, so it seems you can work full-time' - speculation. Source [2] only says 'casual employment for a maximum of 20 hours per week during school term and 40 hours per week during holidays'. Main point (40 hrs in holidays) matches the reference.

question: How many hours can a student work per week during term time
reference: Up to 20 hours per week during term (40 hours per week during the holiday periods).
answer: Students with a valid Stamp 2 permission may work up to 20 hours a week while they are studying in Ireland [2]. During the months of June, July, August and September and from 15 December to 15 January students may work up to 40 hours per week [2].

question: What documents do I need to bring to my first registration appointment
reference: It depends on your stamp. All applicants need certain documents (e.g. passport, proof of address, the relevant visa/landing stamp, medical insurance where required) plus documents specific to their stamp category. A good answer explains this or asks which stamp the person has.
answer:
For a Stamp 2A Registration, you will need to bring:
- The biometric page of your current valid passport(s) [5]
- A letter from your college/school confirming your enrolment as a student [5]
- Proof that you have paid college/school fees [5]
- Private Medical Insurance or Travel Insurance with medical cover for accidents and medical incident including hospital stays in Ireland, valid for 12 months, or if less than 12 months – for the duration of your stay [3, 5]
- Proof of your exam results [5]

For a Stamp 1G Registration, you will need to bring:
- The biometric page of you and your spouse’s/ de facto’s current valid passports [3]
- The relevant permit of your spouse / de facto partner [3]
- Private Medical Insurance or Travel Insurance with medical cover for accidents and medical incident including hospital stays in Ireland, valid for 12 months, or if less than 12 months – for the duration of your stay [3]

For a Stamp 2 Registration, you will need to bring:
- A Mobility Agreement, Learning Agreement, or Inter-institutional Agreement [4]

question: Do I need proof of address to register my immigration permission
reference: Yes. Proof of address is one of the requirements for all registrations and renewals.
answer: Yes, you will need to provide proof of address, which must be dated in the last 3 months [1]. This is a requirement for all registrations and renewals [2].
notes: Says proof of address 'must be dated in the last 3 months [1]'. Source [1] is about proving a NEW address after a change of address (utility bill/tenancy agreement dated in last 3 months), not about registration. Source [2] lists 'Proof of address' with no date rule. Main answer (yes, required) is right.

question: How do I renew my IRP card
reference: Apply online through the ISD online renewals portal, from up to 12 weeks before your IRP expires. You must be in Ireland when you apply.
answer:
You can apply to renew your IRP card up to 12 weeks prior to its expiry date [2]. You must currently be present in Ireland to be eligible to renew your permission to remain online and accept a declaration confirming this when applying [2]. Applications should be submitted online through the online renewals portal [3].

To complete the application, select the Registration (IRP Card) Renewals form, read and accept the declaration and data privacy notice, and enter the required personal information, including your nationality and passport details [4].

question: Can I renew my permission online while I am outside Ireland
reference: No. You must be present in Ireland to renew online; applications submitted from outside Ireland will be rejected.
answer: No, you must be present in Ireland in order to apply to renew your permission online [1]. You must currently be present in Ireland to be eligible to renew your permission to remain online and accept a declaration confirming this when applying. Any applications submitted from outside Ireland will be rejected [4].

question: How long can I be out of the country in a year and keep my registration
reference: Absence from the State should not exceed 90 days in a rolling year.
answer: You can spend up to 90 days outside Ireland in a rolling year without affecting your registration [2]. This includes holidays, personal travel, and work-related absences [1]. If you exceed this limit, it may impact your ability to re-enter the state or renew your permission [4].
notes: Says exceeding 90 days 'may impact your ability to re-enter the state or renew your permission [4]'. Source [4] only says a visa-required national who leaves before their first registration appointment cannot re-enter without a new entry visa; no source states any consequence of exceeding 90 days. Main answer (90 days in a rolling year) matches the reference.

question: How much does the Critical Skills Employment Permit cost
reference: The processing fee is EUR 1,000. If the application is unsuccessful, 90% is refunded.
answer: The processing fee for a Critical Skills Employment Permit is €1,000 [1]. If an application is unsuccessful, 90% of the fee will be refunded to the applicant [1].

question: What is the minimum salary for a critical skills permit if I graduated recently
reference: EUR 36,848 if you received your qualification within the 12 months before applying (otherwise EUR 40,904 for listed occupations).
answer: If you have received your qualification within the 12 month period prior to the date of application for the employment permit, the minimum annual remuneration will be €36,848 [2].

question: How long do I have to stay with my first employer on a critical skills permit
reference: At least 9 months, except in specific circumstances such as redundancy.
answer: You must stay with your initial employer for at least 9 months [1]. However, if you are made redundant, you can seek alternative employment within 6 months of the date of dismissal by reason of redundancy [2, 4].

question: What happens if I am made redundant while on a critical skills permit
reference: Notify the Employment Permits Section within 4 weeks of dismissal. You then have up to 6 months from the date of dismissal to find alternative employment; if not, contact the immigration authorities about your status.
answer:
If you are made redundant while on a Critical Skills Employment Permit, you must notify the Employment Permits Section of the Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment within 4 weeks of your dismissal [1]. You will then have up to 6 months from the date of dismissal by reason of redundancy to seek alternative employment [2]. If you cannot acquire another job within this period, you must contact the immigration authorities to establish your immigration status beyond that period [3].

If you obtain a new job offer with the same job title after being made redundant in a job title that is no longer eligible for a Critical Skills Employment Permit, your application will still be considered [2].

question: When can I move from Stamp 1 to Stamp 4 with a critical skills permit
reference: After completing 21 months of employment on a Critical Skills Employment Permit. Holders apply directly to the Department of Justice for Stamp 4 (no renewal permit or support letter needed).
answer: You can apply directly to the Dept of Justice for a Stamp 4 after your employment permit and immigration registration card expire [1]. You must have been in employment in the State for a minimum of 21 months on the basis of a Critical Skills Employment Permit, and have registered that permission under Stamp 1 conditions [5].
notes: Says 'after your employment permit and immigration registration card expire'; source [1] says holders whose permit and IRP card are 'due to expire' can apply directly to the Dept of Justice. Telling someone to wait until after expiry could leave them without permission. The 21 months is right, but the timing statement is wrong and unsupported.

question: Can my spouse work in Ireland if I hold a critical skills permit
reference: Yes. Once resident, a spouse/partner of a Critical Skills Employment Permit holder can seek employment (e.g. on Stamp 1G without an employment permit, or via a free Dependant/Partner/Spouse Employment Permit).
answer: Yes, once your dependants/partners/spouses are resident in the State, they are eligible to seek any employment [1]. They can also apply for a Dependant/Partner/Spouse Employment Permit, which is currently issued free of charge [1].

question: How soon after arriving in Ireland do I have to register my permission
reference: Within 90 days of arrival, as instructed by the landing stamp in your passport.
answer: You must register your immigration permission within 90 days of arrival in Ireland [1]. You can book a registration appointment as soon as possible after you arrive, and it's recommended that you create an account on the Customer Service Portal and book an appointment at this time [4]. The landing stamp in your passport will instruct you to register with Immigration Service Delivery within 90 days [5].

question: I lost my job through redundancy on a critical skills permit how long do I have to find another one
reference: Up to 6 months from the date of dismissal.
answer: You have up to 6 months from the date of dismissal by reason of redundancy to seek alternative employment [1,2].

question: My employment permit was refused how long do I have to ask for a review
reference: Within 28 days, using the Submission of a Decision for Review form.
answer: You may request a review within 28 days [1]. The review will be considered by a separate and more senior official [1].

question: What happens if I do not send the extra documents they ask for during my renewal
reference: If you do not provide the requested documents within 14 days, your application is refused/closed and you must submit a new application.
answer: If you fail to respond within 14 days with the requested additional documentation, your application will be closed and you will have to submit a new application [1]. There is no further cost involved with submitting further information, but your application will still be closed if you don't comply [1].

question: Can I visit France for a holiday with my Irish IRP card
reference: An IRP card does not by itself allow travel to other EU countries; you must check France's entry requirements before travelling.
answer: According to [2], an IRP does not allow you to travel to or live freely in other EU countries. You should check what you need to enter other countries before you travel, as all existing international travel and immigration rules still apply [2].
